name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This makes keyboard navigation faster by letting users bypass repetitive blocks like headers and nav menus in one click. The trade-off is a small permanent link that takes up space, but its benefits for keyboard users far outweigh the visual clutter for sighted users.

name: Reader
text: A large, always-visible skip link risks layout shift when it appears, pushing content down and breaking sighted users' flow. Instead, make it appear only on keyboard focus—no extra space until needed—and test with Playwright MCP to confirm no unintended shifts.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** that only appears when keyboard focus reaches the top of the page. This keeps the link hidden until needed, preventing layout shifts while still giving keyboard users instant access to skip repetitive blocks. The trade-off is a brief flash of the link when activated, but it’s a small price for making navigation truly usable for everyone. Test with Playwright MCP to confirm no layout shifts occur.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is the flash of the skip link when it appears—it can distract sighted users and break their flow. A better alternative is to make the skip link always visible but tiny (1px by 1px) until focus arrives, then expand it smoothly. Settle it by testing both with Playwright MCP to measure layout shifts and user feedback on distraction.
